label: Circumferential tissue wrap (front-to-sides)

provenance.anchors_note: factor anchors are [E] fits over the [S] pattern: FAT_REFERENCE R2's deposition ordering (abdomen loads first, flanks fifth - the sides LAG the front at low levels) closing to a full ring at heavy classes (R6: the clinical pannus definition includes flanks and back; waist:hip converges 0.98-1.02 at class II-III, i.e. the whole ring fills). Prior art that the sides are a real deposition site, not spillover: HIMBO ships a dedicated LoveHandles block (1,071 diff verts, max |delta| 0.0224 m) and the v4 fat build's flank roll (peak at h 0.28, 10.3 cm pinch contrast, GRAVITY_V4 M7b) was delivered by the learned fields' flank mass
provenance.method: authored coupling record (MUSCLE_TISSUE_MODEL.md section 4, circumferential wrap)

semantics: Fat distributes CIRCUMFERENTIALLY: the tissue field is a ring around the torso, not a patch on the front (Joe, Nov 12, 2026: 'fat goes from front to sides as well, the sides dont stay stiff'). Per band, wrap.factor is the side-sector radial gain the geometry layer must deliver as a fraction of the front-sector gain, piecewise in the band's front tissue: the flanks lag at lean levels and the ring closes at heavy ones. The coupling emits wrap.factor.<band> as the kernel calibration target and, where the profile resolves a true side region (waist band: flanks vs abdomen), wrap.ratio.waist from the resolved regional tissue. STIFF SIDES is a defined failure: side/front ratio below floor_ratio while front tissue is at or above min_front_tissue - at the vector layer it raises an advisory (it guards the regional profile); on a mesh it is a build failure, not a warning. The chest band has no side region at the vector layer, so it emits its factor only; its ratio is a geometry-layer measurement.
